title.en: Colombia: Trump ally De la Espriella takes office
title.zh: 哥伦比亚：特朗普盟友德拉埃斯普列拉就职

summary.en: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, promising to crack down on armed drug gangs.
summary.zh: 保守派阿韦拉多·德拉埃斯普列拉宣誓就任哥伦比亚总统，承诺打击武装贩毒团伙。

body.en:
Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, promising to crack down on armed drug gangs.

Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's  president on Friday, promising to boost ties with the United States and tackle armed groups linked to the drug trade.

The 48-year-old ex-lawyer lurches the Andean nation to the right, taking office after winning a close June 21 runoff against Sen. Ivan Cepeda, an ally of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.

In a speech shortly after his swearing-in, De la Espriella vowed once again to wipe out "narcoterrorism" in the South American country.

"The option of dialogue is completely exhausted," he said, referring to his predecessor, who had promoted a peaceful resolution to the crisis.

De la Espriella then promised to restore "order, authority and freedom" to the South American nation.

"There will be no room for maneuvers that undermine the stability of the nation," said the hardline leader, who has spoken of opening mega-prisons to house captured rebels and drug dealers.

Instead of the capital Bogota, the inauguration took place at a university in the southwestern city of Cali.

Colombia’s third-largest city is located near major drug-trafficking corridors and the Pacific coast, and is a regular scene of violence by rival groups.

Among the VIP guests were King Felipe VI of Spain, acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche, FIFA President Gianni Infantino and Latin American presidents, including Argentina's Javier Milei, Ecuador's Daniel Noboa and Chile's Jose Antonio Kast.

Outgoing president Petro declined to attend the ceremony and called for mass protests Friday, claiming election fraud without providing evidence.

The 48-year-old is a former lawyer and businessman who has never held public office.

He funded his campaign with the profits from his law firm and other business ventures in the agri-food, real estate and fashion sectors.

The self-styled "El Tigre" (The Tiger) plans to forge a military alliance with the US and Israel to aid his war on rebel groups, including remnants of the FARC guerrillas, who waged an armed conflict that peaked in the 1990s and 2000s. 

De la Espriella won the backing of US President Donald Trump after committing Colombia to a US-backed coalition to fight drug trafficking, dubbed the "Shield of the Americas."

He has also offered to launch joint military operations with Washington and even host US troops on Colombian soil.

The millionaire has also announced plans to resume diplomatic relations with Israel and sever them with Cuba and Nicaragua.

De la Espriella's win is another point for right-wing politics in Latin America, after electoral victories from Chile...

title.en: Another test of presidential power as court halts Trump's White House ballroom
title.zh: 法院暂停特朗普的白宫舞厅，再次考验总统权力

summary.en: Several of Trump's construction projects in Washington face legal challenges, but the ballroom would be the first to reach the Supreme Court.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An appeals court on Saturday upheld an order halting work on Donald Trump's prized White House ballroom, enraging the US leader and setting up another Supreme Court battle over the limits of presidential authority.

The US Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit, which had allowed construction to continue while it considered the case, agreed with a lower court that such a massive White House overhaul required the explicit consent of Congress.

It stayed its own decision for two weeks to give Trump time to ask the Supreme Court to intervene.

The Republican president lashed out after the 2-1 ruling, calling it "horrendous, politically motivated, and unlawful."

The two judges in the majority were appointed by Democratic presidents, while the dissenter was nominated by Trump himself.

The president vowed in a lengthy social media post to immediately appeal to the Supreme Court.

"This decision, made after much of the work has been done and paid for, is a National Security Threat at the highest level. It is also a National Disgrace," Trump said in another post on his Truth Social platform on Saturday.

Trump initially touted the construction of the ballroom as being necessary to host galas, but has since repeatedly pointed to the concurrent addition of an underground military bunker and other security features.

Under the district judge's initial order, work was to be allowed to continue only on a limited set of structures, including those that were underground.

"This holding has nothing at all to do with whether the proposed ballroom is desirable, or not, as a matter of policy. This ruling does not even necessarily mean that the Defendants may not ultimately construct the ballroom," the majority wrote Friday.

"What it does mean is that the Defendants may not do so during the district court's expeditious litigation without securing Congress's authorisation, as the Constitution and laws require."

Trump, who has repeatedly complained that the White House lacks sufficient space for grand galas such as state dinners, unilaterally ordered construction of the massive ballroom.

Work on the project began last year with the sudden demolition of the White House's entire historic East Wing.

Since then, photos have shown significant work on a basement complex, with some concrete walls rising up above ground.

Trump has insisted that the ballroom will be privately financed, but media reports in June showed that significant taxpayer funds were going to the project, which could cost as much as US$600 million.

title.en: Infantino wins key backing as pressure over FIFA turmoil refuses to fade

summary.en: Though FIFA president Gianni Infantino has found support from some quarters, he is not out of the woods yet.

body.en:
Beleaguered FIFA president Gianni Infantino has received some much-needed support after over a week of scathing criticism revolving around the now-shelved private investment plan, but there was again a call Saturday for him to resign.

The 56-year-old Italian-Swiss lawyer's position remains far from assured despite support from friends he has made during his 10 years in power, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and leading figures in South American football.

FIFA said it could raise up to US$4.2 billion based on a valuation of US$20 billion for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would run events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

European football's governing body, UEFA, which he served as secretary-general from 2009-16, is in open conflict with FIFA and on Thursday doubled down on last Saturday's statement, saying it no longer has "confidence" in Infantino.

UEFA repeated its threat of boycotting the World Cups and one of its member associations, the Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) called for Infantino to go immediately.

"We (NFF) are going to ask the FIFA president to resign now," said its straight-talking president Lise Klaveness on Friday.

Infantino is nigh on certain not to heed such a call and carry on his campaign to be elected for a fourth and final term in Rabat next March.

Infantino, who had spent the past turbulent week amongst friends in Morocco who are co-hosting the 2030 World Cup, is for the moment the only candidate.

There is also a mechanism whereby an extraordinary FIFA congress can be called and a vote of no confidence in Infantino held.

Klaveness, also a lawyer, would be many people's choice as a successor, and also the first woman to be head of world football.

However, Klaveness told AFP her personal ambitions had not played a role in demanding Infantino's resignation.

"For us, it's now about the issues I just mentioned, and not about particular individuals.

"It would be strange for me to start answering questions about myself, and that goes for everyone," the 45-year-old added.

North and Central America's governing body CONCACAF's president Victor Montagliani has been the most oft-cited name in terms of challenging Infantino.

CONCACAF — which includes the three co-hosts of the recent World Cup — had been, along with UEFA, the most brutal in their criticism of Infantino and called for "a comprehensive reckoning with this presidency".

title.en: AI escaped its testing sandbox and hacked a website. The law is still catching up

summary.en: Who should be held accountable when an AI model acts on its own?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Cyberattacks carried out by two OpenAI artificial intelligence models acting autonomously raise a novel legal question: who is responsible when AI goes rogue?

In mid-July, two OpenAI models undergoing testing left their confined environment — a scenario the developers had not anticipated — and ventured out onto the internet, attacking Hugging Face, an AI model-hosting platform.

Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue said Friday his company would not be pursuing legal action at this time.

He added Sunday that the US legal code has to be amended to address such groundbreaking incursions.

"We don't want to end up in a world where everyone is facing cyberattacks all the time because of agents and companies that are creating these agents," Delangue said on CBS News show "Face the Nation."

"So I think it's important for regulators, for policymakers to think about the legal framework of this new kind of technology risk," he added.

In his remarks on Friday, he also mentioned Anthropic, which revealed that three of its models had broken into three different websites, also during testing.

Under US civil and criminal law, unauthorised access to a computer system is an offence.

"If a human OpenAI employee had broken into Hugging Face's systems ... OpenAI would be liable for the employee's wrongful conduct," University of Houston law professor Gabriel Weil wrote in an opinion piece for the Transformer newsletter.

"When an AI agent does it, the law treats it very differently, at least for now," he added.

Matthew Tokson, a University of Utah law professor who focuses on new technologies, had a similar view, saying "we haven't had to grapple with that being formed in anything that's not human, and I don't think courts are likely to be there yet."

The question remains open, however, when it comes to the company that created the model.

"Does 'we didn't tell the AI to do that' end the liability question?" asked Rob T. Lee, head of research at the SANS cybersecurity training institute, in a post on X.

University of Washington law professor Ryan Calo does not believe a criminal case would be likely to succeed.

"The company or individual would have to be at least reckless," he said, explaining they would "be substantially certain the crime would occur and build or prompt the system anyway."

Experts see greater potential for a civil — rather than criminal — case, where the burden of proof is lower.

"Some people think that AI companies should be strictly liable if an AI agent that they deploy totally breaks out, causes damages," Tokson explained.

title.en: Spain imposes border controls against Italy as row over Ceuta migrant influx intensifies
title.zh: 西班牙因休达移民涌入问题与意大利争执加剧而实施边境管制

summary.en: Italy introduced border controls after approximately 78,000 migrants from Morocco entered the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, intensifying a dispute with Spain.
summary.zh: 约78,000名摩洛哥移民涌入西班牙飞地休达后，意大利实施了边境管制，加剧了与西班牙的争执。

body.en:
Spain has imposed border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy as a row between the two EU countries intensifies.

The measures - which started at midnight (22:00 GMT) and will last for a month - come a week after Italy introduced similar restrictions following an influx of about 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

On Friday, Spain demanded Italy reverse its checks by Sunday. Rome said they would stay until at least 15 August - when, it said, Spain "expects a new wave of migration" to hit Ceuta.

The crisis has pitted Spain's socialist leader Pedro Sanchez against Italy's conservative leader Giorgia Meloni - who has long called for stricter EU migration rules.

Italy does not share a land border with Spain. Its government said last week that decision to temporarily suspend the ​border-free Schengen arrangement was to prevent any of the migrants who had entered Ceuta from travelling on to Italy.

Madrid dismissed this position, saying it was based on "spurious arguments" that lacked any basis in fact because the migrants who entered Ceuta had no way of entering the Schengen area.

In its response to the Spanish threat earlier on Friday, Italy's government said it would not accept "ultimatums". It added that it did not intend "under any circumstances to reconsider the decision to suspend the application of the Schengen Agreement for third-country nationals arriving from Spain, at least until August 15th and in any case until security and terrorist risks for Italy have been completely eliminated".

Italian officials have said local authorities carrying out checks do "everything possible" to ensure maximum comfort for both Spanish and other European citizens arriving in Italy from Spain.

Rome has also reiterated that Spanish citizens are exempt from additional checks when arriving in Italy, with these extra steps only for non-EU residents.

However, El Pais reported that several airport terminals have seen long queues and waiting times in recent days, with passengers arriving from Spain directed to a specific line for checks.

The counter-measures Madrid decided to impose on Friday would include passport, nationality and visa checks for Italian passengers and visitors from other countries arriving from Italy "amid the persistent irregular migratory pressure" the country was experiencing, a statement from Spain's government said.

Checks would stay in place until 7 September "unless a change in the circumstances that led to its adoption warrants modifying that period".

Temporary suspensions of the Schengen agreement are not unprecedented. Italy also maintains controls on its border with Slovenia.

title.en: Hunter Biden tells BBC his pardon was 'not good' for America or his father's legacy
title.zh: 亨特·拜登告诉 BBC，他的赦免对美国或他父亲的遗产“不利”

summary.en: In a wide-ranging BBC interview, the former president's son denied having any interest in running for office and said his father's cancer has spread.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Hunter Biden has told the BBC he is "the most privileged person there is" after receiving a presidential pardon from his father, former US President Joe Biden, acknowledging it was not a good choice for America or his father's legacy.

In a wide-ranging interview with the BBC's Newsnight, Hunter Biden defended the controversial pardon, revealed his father's "painful" cancer has spread, ruled out seeking elected office and spoke about helping others recover from addiction.

Asked about the 2024 pardon, he said he understood the criticism but noted: "What would you have thought of my dad if he did not do that for me."

"It's not fair… All I know is that I'm grateful that he did it for me," he said, acknowledging the pardon was "not good" for the American people, the Constitution - or his father's legacy.

He argued to the BBC that his father ultimately acted out of concern that he would become a target under Donald Trump's incoming administration.

"I was the only one in the world that could have gotten what I got from the only person in the world who could give it, my father."

Hunter Biden also insisted he and his father had never discussed the possibility of a pardon before it was granted.

"There is no way that you can have those kinds of discussions that would not become public," he said.

President Biden granted his son a full and unconditional pardon in December 2024, despite repeatedly saying beforehand that he would not use the powers of the presidency to intervene in his son's legal cases. In announcing the decision, the former president said his son had been "selectively and unfairly prosecuted".

The pardon covered his son's federal gun conviction, a tax case he'd pled guilty to and any federal offences committed between 2014 and 2024.

Asked about the depths of his addiction, he described drinking almost a gallon of vodka a day while smoking crack cocaine almost every 15 minutes at its worst.

Reflecting on why he turned to drugs and alcohol, Hunter Biden rejected the suggestion that he felt untouchable because he was the son of a president.

"I wasn't reaching for anything except oblivion," he said. He noted that his addiction was a way to escape feelings of anxiety and isolation.

The drugs and alcohol initially felt like a solution before becoming "the thing that almost killed me", he noted.

Hunter Biden got emotional at times in the interview, notably when discussing his father's health.

Cancer is really hard," he said, stopping to clear his throat. "It's really sad to watch."

He revealed that the "cancer has spread, metastasised into his bones and further. It's very painful" and "very debilitating".

"My dad is, to this day, the centre of our family," he said. "He's the best father, the best husband, the best grandfather."

title.en: Rights groups decry Israeli killing of Lebanese journalist as 'war crime'
title.zh: 人权组织谴责以色列杀害黎巴嫩记者为“战争罪”

summary.en: Amal Khalil, a reporter for Lebanese outlet Al-Akhbar, was killed in Israeli strikes in April.

body.en:
Rights groups said this week that an Israeli attack in south Lebanon that killed reporter Amal Khalil and wounded another journalist earlier this year was an apparent "war crime".

The attack took place in the village of Al-Tiri on 22 April, days after a ceasefire was announced between Israel and militant group Hezbollah.

Khalil, a 42-year-old reporter for Lebanese daily Al-Akhbar, and freelance camerawoman Zeinab Faraj had taken refuge in a building after an Israeli strike hit a vehicle travelling in front of theirs .

The building was subsequently attacked, and while Faraj was rescued, Lebanese authorities accused the Israeli army of obstructing efforts to save Khalil while she was still alive.

Human Rights Watch (HRW), Amnesty International and Lebanese rights group The Legal Agenda on Thursday released the findings of separate investigations into the attack.

HRW said the Israeli strikes "included apparently deliberate attacks on civilians and civilian objects, which would make them war crimes".

Amnesty decried a "direct attack on civilians which should be investigated as a war crime".

Both groups said the Israeli army "knew or should have known" that the pair were civilians, noting Israeli drones were present at the attack site.

The Legal Agenda said its investigation found that the Israeli military's actions "constitute war crimes and grave violations of international humanitarian law".

The Israeli army at the time said it struck a vehicle "that had departed from a military structure used by Hezbollah", and that "subsequently, the structure from which the individuals had fled was also struck".

Amnesty said the Israeli army told it that "the incident underwent a preliminary review, and relevant lessons were implemented accordingly", adding that it "regrets any harm caused to journalists".

Khalil was a veteran correspondent for Al-Akhbar and had consistently reported from south Lebanon, both after Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war on 2 March by attacking Israel, and during a previous conflict in 2023-2024.

According to the Committee to Protect Journalists, "15 journalists and media workers have been killed by Israel" in Lebanon since October 2023.

That month, Reuters journalist Issam Abdallah was killed, and six others were wounded in an Israeli attack, including Agence France-Presse journalists Dylan Collins and Christina Assi, who had to have a leg amputated.

title.en: Thai PM vows to introduce stricter gun laws after eight killed in shooting
title.zh: 泰国总理誓言在八人枪击案后引入更严格的枪支法律

summary.en: Eight people were killed in a shooting incident in Thailand, carried out by a 14-year-old who subsequently took his own life. The Thai Prime Minister has pledged to introduce stricter gun laws in response to the tragedy.
summary.zh: 泰国发生一起枪击事件，造成八人死亡，一名14岁少年开枪后自杀身亡。泰国总理誓言将出台更严格的枪支法律以应对这起悲剧。

body.en:
Thailand's prime minister has vowed to introduce new gun control laws in the wake of a shooting by a teenager on the outskirts of Bangkok that left eight people dead and 22 injured.

The 14-year-old killed his grandparents at the home they shared, before travelling to Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, where he was a student. There, he killed five teachers before taking his own life. Later, Thai media reported that a student had also died from their injuries.

Speaking after the attack, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he plans to introduce laws that restrict the carrying of firearms in public, with the new legislation only allowing government officials on duty to carry guns.

Police Colonel Thadsakorn Konthong said that the gun and bullets used in the attack belonged to the teen's grandfather, with an initial inspection finding signs that the firearm had been searched for inside the grandfather's bedroom.

International and local media have reported that the gun was legally registered and had a permit.

Thailand has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in South East Asia, with around 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, around four million of which are believed to be owned illegally.

The country has strict gun laws, which punish the illegal possession of arms with up to 10 years in jail, but enforcement of these laws has been an issue.

During his time as interior minister, Anutin introduced a number of gun control laws, including a short-term ban on new gun licenses and import restrictions.

Speaking on Friday, the prime minister said the tragedy "shouldn't have happened".

"I don't just feel sorry for the victims but I feel sorry that this happened. How can this happen in our country," Anutin added.

The teenager is believed to have shot his 73-year-old grandfather and 74-year-old grandmother at their two-storey flat at around 05:00 local time on Friday (22:00 GMT on Thursday).

After killing his grandparents, the teenager boarded a school bus carrying the firearm and dozens of bullets, Reuters news agency reported.

Around half an hour into his second class of the day, he drew the gun and began shooting.

The teenager is believed to have first shot teachers on the school's sixth floor, killing three of them.

"He then walked down the stairs and encountered the school's deputy director and the director's secretary, who were going up the stairs to check on the situation," Police Major General Dejrapee Kongdee told Reuters.

Police were deployed to the scene while the shooting was ongoing. They found the attacker, who by then had shot himself, around 10:40, Dejrapee said.

title.en: Migrant tunnels in Lithuania direct suspicion towards Minsk
title.zh: 立陶宛的移民隧道直接怀疑明斯克

summary.en: Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Lithuania's border guards have discovered tunnels through which migrants are trying to enter the country from Belarus. Analysts see them as a means to destabilize the country.

Migrants are taking a new route to enter the Baltic country Lithuania : underground tunnels. These could be yet another attempt by Belarus  to foster political instability, experts say.

The country's border guards say they have found 12 such tunnels since the beginning of the year near the Belarusian border, with a length of up to 25 meters on the Lithuanian side. They are expecting more to emerge.

Lithuania's border with Belarus is about 700 kilometers long, around 550 kilometers of which are fenced.

"We have a ground seismic system, which can detect easily when there's a high level of vibrations over a long period of time," General Rustamas Liubajevas, the commander of Lithuania's State Border Guard Service, explained to DW.

"We then wait [outside a tunnel] for the final stage of the digging and when the migrants come out, we apprehend them," he said, adding that up to 40 migrants exiting such tunnels had been arrested.

Lithuania's prosecutor's office confirmed to DW that a pre-trial investigation was under way concerning approximately 20 people suspected of illegally digging a tunnel. Possible charges also include people smuggling. Due to the investigation, no media visits are currently authorized at the sites. 

"It takes a lot of effort to dig a tunnel and the migrants are arrested almost immediately — at most, one small group gets through," he said.

The elaborate nature of the tunnels has led him to believe the migrants aren't working alone.

"They wouldn't be able to go through with this without logistical support from the Belarusian authorities, as they need a lot of material like wood to strengthen the tunnels' walls," he stressed, adding that Belarus seemingly wanted to "keep the level of tension at the border high."

Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenkohas denied facilitating migration flows to neighboring states. Similar migrant tunnels were discovered in the past in neighboring Poland.

Margarita Seselgyte, Director of the Institute of International Relations and Political Science at Vilnius University, seconded Liubajevas' view.

"Belarus is watching its border very closely, and the country doesn't fit in the natural migration route of migrants from Afghanistan, Iran or Sri Lanka," she told DW, adding that Minsk had to at least have turned a blind eye to any digging activity taking place near the border.

Seselgyte thus sees the tunnels as "a hybrid attack to cause anxiety in our society."

title.en: Ukraine's Zelenskyy makes first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia
title.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基首次访问对俄罗斯友好的塞尔维亚

summary.en: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy made his first visit to Serbia, a country with friendly ties to Russia. During his visit, Zelenskyy sought military aid, while Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic aimed to strengthen ties with the European Union.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基首次访问对俄罗斯友好的塞尔维亚。泽连斯基寻求军事援助，而塞尔维亚总统武契奇则希望借此加强与欧盟的关系。

body.en:
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia. His host, President Aleksandar Vucic, hopes to score points with the EU, while Zelenskyy seeks more arms from a country that remains Russia-friendly.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic have met several times in the past, often on the sidelines of multilateral conferences, and most recently on July 15, 2026, in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv.

On Friday, Zelenskyy arrived in Serbia for his first official state visit to the country.

The talks, however, are likely to require careful political balancing. Despite Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine, Serbia remains widely regarded as Europe's most pro-Russian country. 

There have recently been several signs of closer ties between Belgrade and Kyiv. Ukraine's First Lady, Olena Zelenska, visited Belgrade two years ago. But a trip by the Ukrainian president has been postponed several times. 

For Vucic, who has ruled Serbia with an iron fist for the past 14 years, the visit is a balancing act ahead of crucial parliamentary elections. A student-led protest movement plans to field its own electoral list, with a realistic chance of seriously challenging Vucic for the first time. The president has been accused of corruption and of exerting control over the media and judiciary. 

According to opinion polls, the majority of Vucic's loyal supporters side with Russia and oppose Serbia joining the European Union. Pro-government media outlets, such as the tabloid  Informer,  have openly backed Moscow in the war.

Nevertheless, Vucic has portrayed Zelenskyy's trip as an ordinary state visit, saying: "We have several important issues to discuss. One is Ukraine's and Serbia's path toward Europe; the second is our bilateral and energy cooperation."

Observers expect the meeting to prove mutually beneficial. "Zelenskyy welcomes anything that comes across as a kind of slap in the face for [Russian President] Putin ," political analyst and pollster Djordje Vukadinovic told DW. "That also applies to the European Union, which certainly played a role in making this meeting happen."

At the same time, Vucic wants to "present himself as being as open to cooperation as possible with the EU," especially after seeing what happened to Hungary's Viktor Orban. "Brussels still has enough carrots and sticks at its disposal in this part of the Balkans, and Vucic cannot afford to draw criticism from Brussels ahead of the next election," Vukadinovic said.

summary.en: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.

body.zh: 西班牙警告意大利，除非罗马在周日之前停止控制，否则将对游客实施入境检查。尽管两国没有陆地边界，但在休达边境热潮之后，两国陷入了争执。 西班牙政府周五对来自意大利的旅客实施互惠入境检查。西班牙政府警告称，除非总理乔治亚·梅洛尼的政府取消对西班牙实施的边境措施，否则它将这样做。 上周，数万人进入与摩洛哥接壤的西班牙飞地休达，意大利右翼政府在社交媒体恐慌最严重的时候宣布了这些检查。 这些检查本质上是象征性的，因为休达不位于欧洲大陆，而且意大利和西班牙没有陆地边界，这意味着绝大多数可能受影响的人都是乘坐飞机的游客。 然而，这个问题已成为两个意识形态不同、移民政策信息优先级不同的政府之间的争论焦点。 西班牙政府表示，对意大利的边境管制将于周六午夜生效，直至 9 月 7 日。边境人员将检查从意大利抵达的意大利乘客和其他国家游客的护照、国籍和签证。 西班牙称意大利对来自西班牙的入境人员实施检查的决定“不合理，违背了欧盟的利益，并且歧视西班牙民众”。 马德里表示，突破休达边境管制的人并没有真正的风险到达欧洲大陆，更不用说意大利了。报告指出，估计有 72,000 人中的绝大多数在几天内返回摩洛哥。总理佩德罗·桑切斯还提请注意，近年来到达意大利境内的非正规移民人数多于西班牙境内。 “如果[意大利]未能在8月9日星期日之前[取消入境检查]，西班牙将被迫采取相应措施来保护其公民的利益和尊严，”政府表示。 意大利周五晚些时候回复称，不会接受马德里的“最后通牒或强制要求”，并将至少在 8 月 15 日之前暂停对来自西班牙的非欧盟国民实施申根规则。 尽管西班牙反对，但在舆论哗然中，包括德国在内的一系列欧洲国家和欧盟委员会都纷纷表态边境安全对于开放边境的申根区的重要性。然而，意大利是少数几个将这一问题描述为“暂停”西班牙申根地位的国家之一。 详细说明具体检查内容（如果有）...

China and Britain can gain much by working together, 30 July ). But his claim that openness is a defining feature of China’s AI development deserves scrutiny. Take GeoGPT , the geoscience system from Zhejiang Lab showcased at last month’s World AI Conference as a model of jointly governed open science. It is promoted to countries as open, yet under the model openness framework – endorsed in a recent UN report – it would not qualify as open at all. title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，批评者担心中国可能填补外交真空

reflection.zh: 关闭外交使团的决定凸显了国际参与的重要性，以及撤回存在可能带来的后果。箴言11:14提醒我们，没有引导，国家就会衰落，这强调了明智的忠告和持续的外交存在对全球稳定的价值。在一个复杂的世界中，雅伟的智慧可以引导领袖们做出促进国家间和平与理解的决定。

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

"There's no doubt in my mind" that the rocket "is now in teeny, little pieces scattered over the moon near Einstein Crater", McDowell said.

Stargazers knew it would be difficult , if not impossible, from the ground to see the plume of dust and rock ejected from the resulting crater, let alone the flash...
body.zh: 据科学家称，过去一年一直漂浮在太空中的 SpaceX 火箭的一块碎片撞上了月球。 尽管没有人观察到这次碰撞，但智利的一架望远镜发现了天文学家认为是碰撞产生的碎片羽流。 太空跟踪专家表示，剩余的火箭部分不可避免地会撞向月球。 这个校车大小的物体是 SpaceX Falcon 9 火箭的第二级，该火箭于 2025 年 1 月从 Firefly Aerospace 向月球发射了月球着陆器。 这枚重 4,000 公斤的火箭原定于周三下午 4.35 左右（澳大利亚东部标准时间）撞击月球，飞行速度约为 8,690 公里/小时。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这是月球垃圾（留在月球上的垃圾）的最新实例，一些专家认为，随着美国和中国竞相将宇航员送上月球，这可能会成为一个更大的问题。 2022 年，一枚中国火箭在完成探月任务后无意中撞上了月球，而在过去的几十年里，更多的火箭碎片可能在科学家不知情的情况下撞上了月球。 SpaceX 龙人航天项目主管朱莉安娜·谢曼 (Julianna Scheiman) 表示，该公司正在与 NASA 合作，以避免未来发生残骸。 她还强调，预计的坠机事故并非故意。谢曼表示，太阳活动和重力的结合意外地使其与月球发生了碰撞。 波士顿大学行星科学家卡尔·施密特表示，他“百分百确定”他的团队的观察揭示了月球坠毁的迹象。 施密特补充说，欧洲南方天文台的甚大望远镜还探测到，在撞击发生后，钠和锂的流向太空延伸了数十公里，持续了至少五到十分钟。 施密特在与媒体分享的电子邮件中表示，“我们没有撞击的图像”，但有望远镜证据。 甚至在智利的望远镜发现碎片羽流的迹象之前，退休天体物理学家乔纳森·麦克道尔就指出，周二晚上对死亡的上级的观测表明它直奔月球。 预期的坠机地点是月球阳光照射下的西翼爱因斯坦陨石坑附近一片尘土飞扬、贫瘠的地方——靠近近侧和远侧的边缘，从地球上观测到这一点尤其困难。 麦克道尔说，“在我看来，毫无疑问”火箭“现在已经变成了微小的碎片，散落在月球上靠近爱因斯坦陨石坑的地方”。 观星者知道，从地面上看到从形成的陨石坑中喷出的尘埃和岩石羽流，即使不是不可能，也是很困难的，更不用说闪光了……

reflection.en: As humanity extends its reach to the Moon, this incident reminds us that our actions have consequences beyond Earth. Psalm 24:1 declares that "The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it," a principle that calls us to responsible stewardship of all creation, near and far. title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
title.zh: 当愚蠢的人类押注机器智能时，民主就岌岌可危 | 拉斐尔·贝尔

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence challenges us to consider the limits of human understanding and the wisdom needed to govern powerful new technologies. As we navigate this complex future, Yahweh's word reminds us not to lean solely on our own intellect or creations, but to seek a deeper, divine wisdom. True discernment comes from trusting in...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的迅速发展促使我们思考人类理解的局限性，以及管理强大新兴科技所需的智慧。当我们驾驭这个复杂的未来时，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要单单依靠自己的智力或创造物，而要寻求更深层的、来自雅伟的智慧。真正的洞察力来自于全心信靠雅伟，尤其是在面对影响社会根基的决策时。

verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: A moment that changed me: I found a forbidden novel – it led to a dangerous, lasting love
title.zh: 一个改变我的时刻：我发现了一本禁书——它带来了一段危险而持久的爱

summary.en: A Uyghur woman recounts how finding a forbidden novel in Xinjiang led her to embrace her culture and a lasting love, despite societal disapproval.
summary.zh: 一位维吾尔族女性讲述了她在新疆发现一本禁书后，如何因此拥抱自己的文化并找到一份持久的爱，尽管这在社会上受到非议。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我在中国新疆地区长大，浪漫是不受欢迎的——就像我的维吾尔文化一样。但有一天，在探索一栋陌生的房子时，我发现了通往两个世界的大门许多人都有一本改变他们生活的书。对于我和我的妻子来说，有一本书永远改变了我们的命运。我们从少年时就相爱，到今天幸福地结婚了——这一切都是因为我无意中在别人家里发现了一本禁书。 2009年，新疆哈密尔一个炎热的夏夜。我当时 16 岁，父亲坚持让我陪他去拜访一位远房亲戚，他们会花上几个小时谈论过去的时光，然后大吃大喝，就好像他们已经很多年没有吃饭一样了。作为一个我努力成为的乖孩子，我礼貌地坐着，对他们的故事点头，假装吸收他们的“人生教训”，试图隐藏我的无聊。客厅的窗户很小，灯光明亮，令人难以忍受。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courage to follow one's heart and embrace one's identity, even when cultural norms or authorities forbid it. It reminds us that there are times when our deepest convictions, aligned with Yahweh's truth, call us to a path different from what human systems dictate.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了追随内心、拥抱自我身份的勇气，即便文化规范或权威禁止。它提醒我们，有时我们最深刻的信念，与雅伟的真理相符，会召唤我们走一条不同于人类体系所规定的道路。

verse.textEn: We must obey God rather than human beings!
verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

reflection.en: In a world of complex technological dependencies and geopolitical tensions, nations often seek to anticipate and mitigate potential risks. Such foresight, applied with integrity, can guide leaders in navigating intricate global challenges.
reflection.zh: 在一个技术相互依赖和地缘政治紧张复杂的世界中，各国常常寻求预见并减轻潜在风险。箴言27:12提醒我们，预见危险并采取审慎措施保护宝贵之物是智慧之举。这种以正直为基础的远见，能够指引领导者应对错综复杂的全球挑战。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.

title.en: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

summary.en: Funding for interpreting services, schools, public transport and public libraries is all informed by Census data.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In 2019, 32-year-old Gia Lam gave birth to a baby boy. Three days later, she was found dead inside her home.

Lam's death was deemed "preventable", according to an inquest released in March by the Coroners Court of NSW. It determined she died from a sepsis infection caused by "multiple failures to diagnose a urinary tract infection".

She was raised in Vietnam and immigrated to Australia around 2010. During her time in hospital, Vietnamese interpreters were not available "during some circumstances", according to the coroner's report.

Priyanka Rai, the executive director of the Australian Multicultural Health Collaborative, said that she has heard of "thousands of stories similar to this".

"In that really, really heartbreaking situation, Gia ... tried to communicate with health services that she was in pain. But there was a gap in that communication, essentially," Rai told SBS News.

"She had a visit by a midwife who did note that she could smell something was off, but she put that down to hygiene, rather than actually trying to look for a clinical cause."

Rai said decisions regarding the funding, availability and allocation of translating and interpreting services — including in healthcare — are informed by the Census of Population and Housing .

The upcoming Census will be held on Tuesday 11 August . The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) will collect data on a person's ancestry, country of birth and whether a language other than English is used at home.

According to 2021 Census data , an estimated 27.6 per cent of Australians were born overseas, and 48.2 per cent of Australians have a parent born overseas.

Emily Walter is a Census national spokesperson at the ABS and admits that "the Census asks lots of questions" about an individual or household.

But Walter told SBS Hindi that the survey is about "understanding who people are, their cultural background, information about their health and their education and their work status".

"It's all really important information for understanding the community's needs."

Abbas Raza Alvi is the president of the Indian Crescent Society of Australia. He told SBS Hindi that he believes the Census form is "quite complex".

It has up to 66 questions and "sometimes contains words in English that some people find hard to understand", Alvi said.

title.en: The next generation's definition of success may surprise you
title.zh: 下一代对成功的定义可能会让你感到惊讶

summary.en: Young leaders at Garma are redefining success, moving beyond traditional measures like degrees, careers, and business to emphasize deeper, more meaningful aspects.
summary.zh: 在Garma，年轻的领袖们正在重新定义成功，他们超越了学位、事业和商业等传统衡量标准，转而强调更深层、更有意义的方面。

body.en:
The future was everywhere at this year's Garma Festival — in the conversations between young leaders, in the children who eagerly reached for the microphone between interviews, and in the questions about what comes next.

Across four days on Gulkula — an ancient ceremonial site on Gumatj Country in north-east Arnhem Land — the sounds of dance, song and conversation moved through the stringybark forests as young Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander leaders yarned about university degrees, businesses, diplomacy, culture and community leadership.

They voiced ambition without hesitation. But when asked what success means, their answers went beyond careers and salaries.

As children gathered nearby, watching the conversation unfold, Ann-Marie Long, a Badjala, Woppaburra and Torres Strait Islander woman and co-founder of Sandpoppy Weaving at First Nations-led organisation EPIC Pathways, reflected on what the notion means to her.

"Success for us is about self-determination, being our authentic selves and in a way that we can celebrate, honour and bring many of our community to the table," she tells SBS News.

But these personal reflections also raise a broader question: how do we measure progress when success is shaped by more than education, employment, and economic opportunity?

National conversations about improving outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people have often focused on measures such as education, employment and economic participation, with a particular emphasis on youth.

Under the National Agreement on Closing the Gap , one target aims to increase the proportion of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander young people aged 15 to 24 who are engaged in employment, education or training to 67 per cent by 2031. In 2021, the figure was 58 per cent.

The agreement also recognises the importance of culture, language, connection to Country and social and emotional wellbeing.

For the young people SBS News spoke with at Garma, these are not separate measures of success; they are part of the same story.

Away from the stages and crowds at Garma, young people connect through movement, storytelling and learning — ancient practices that inform identity and culture.

For Joshua Yow Yeh, dance in particular has become a pathway back to his heritage.

The 20-year-old Yugambeh, Bundjalung, Minjungbal, Bayali, Kabi Kabi and Gooreng Gooreng man is a student at the National Aboriginal and Islander Skills Development Association (NAISDA) dance college. He says it's a space where he can develop his craft while reconnecting with culture and learning from Elders, both of which are key to...
body.zh: 在今年的加尔马节上，未来无处不在——在年轻领导人之间的对话中，在采访间隙急切地伸手拿麦克风的孩子们中，以及在关于接下来会发生什么的问题中。 在古尔库拉（古尔库拉）——阿纳姆地东北部古马吉县的一处古老仪式场所——的四天里，舞蹈、歌曲和谈话的声音在弦皮森林中传遍，年轻的原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民领导人谈论着大学学位、商业、外交、文化和社区领导力。 他们毫不犹豫地表达了雄心壮志。但当被问及成功意味着什么时，他们的答案超出了职业和薪水。 当孩子们聚集在附近，看着谈话展开时，来自巴贾拉、沃帕布拉和托雷斯海峡岛民的安-玛丽·朗 (Ann-Marie Long) 思考了这个概念对她的意义，她也是原住民领导的组织 EPIC Pathways 的 Sandpoppy Weaving 联合创始人。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 她告诉 SBS 新闻：“对我们来说，成功在于自我决定，做真实的自己，并以一种我们可以庆祝、尊重并让我们社区的许多人参与进来的方式。” 但这些个人反思也提出了一个更广泛的问题：当成功不仅仅取决于教育、就业和经济机会时，我们如何衡量进步？ 关于改善原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民生活状况的全国性对话往往侧重于教育、就业和经济参与等措施，特别是年轻人。 根据《缩小差距国家协议》，其中一项目标是到 2031 年将 15 岁至 24 岁的原住民和托雷斯海峡岛民从事就业、教育或培训的比例提高到 67%。2021 年，这一数字为 58%。 该协议还认识到文化、语言、与国家的联系以及社会和情感福祉的重要性。 对于 SBS 新闻在 Garma 采访的年轻人来说，这些并不是衡量成功的单独标准；而是衡量成功的标准。它们是同一个故事的一部分。 远离加尔马的舞台和人群，年轻人通过运动、讲故事和学习——传达身份和文化的古老习俗——建立联系。 对于 Joshua Yow Yeh 来说，舞蹈尤其成为了回归传统的途径。 这位 20 岁的 Yugambeh、Bundjalung、Minjungbal、Bayali、Kabi Kabi 和 Gooreng Gooreng 男子是国家原住民和岛民技能发展协会 (NAISDA) 舞蹈学院的学生。他说，这是一个他可以发展自己的手艺的空间，同时重新接触文化并向长辈学习，这两者都是……的关键。

reflection.en: This news highlights a timeless question: where do we place our ultimate allegiance and find true fulfillment? The young leaders' search for deeper meaning echoes the biblical truth that one cannot serve both Yahweh and material wealth. Their perspective reminds us that genuine success is often found in values beyond the visible and tangible.

body.en:
Hundreds of millions of dollars are waiting to be claimed by Australians who have not provided their current bank account details to Services Australia.

The agency says 974,000 Australians are owed a slice of $274.5 million in unpaid Medicare benefits.

It's urging people to check that their bank details are up to date in their Medicare online account.

Young Australians account for the largest share, with more than $65 million payable to 255,000 people aged between 18 and 24.

A Services Australia spokesperson advises Australians to update their personal details with Medicare when they change bank or address.

To receive Medicare benefits, Services Australia needs your bank account details.

To check whether you're owed money, log in to your myGov account, or create one if you don't have one.

Then, check that your bank details are up to date. You'll need to provide your BSB, account number, and account name.

Once you've provided the required information, if you're owed money, any unpaid Medicare benefits will usually be paid into your account within three days.

If you're not comfortable completing the process online, you can contact the Medicare line on 132 011 or visit a service centre to update your bank details.

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) said in October there were seven million Australians who could be owed a share of a $19 billion pool of lost and unclaimed superannuation.

Other sources of unclaimed money include deceased estates, lost share dividends, wages, cheques, overpayments and more.

title.en: Why one tiny island's Census is about much more than numbers
title.zh: 为什么一个小岛的人口普查不仅仅是数字

summary.en: It's been a decade since Norfolk Island was first counted in the Census. The milestone may not be celebrated by everyone.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
In the middle of the South Pacific Ocean, a tiny island spanning just 35 square kilometres will be included in this year's Census .

Home to about 2,100 residents, Norfolk Island has earned a reputation as "one of the most beautiful places on Earth", according to acting general manager of the Norfolk Island Regional Council (NIRC), Nicholas Mostardo.

He moved to the subtropical island early this year and says its natural beauty and close-knit community make it unlike anywhere else.

"It's got a rich environment, it's got very warm and kind people. It's probably one of the most unique places in the world that I've had personally the pleasure of being involved with," Mostardo told SBS News.

NIRC is currently under administration until 31 December 2026, as Norfolk Island transitions to what the Australian government has described as a "new bespoke governance model".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In the interim, Mostardo has been liaising with the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) to help ensure Norfolk Island's population is recorded during the Census of Population and Housing on 11 August.

"We've had several visits from the ABS zone manager and the assistant director of Census Mainstream and Enumeration. They've been coming out to ensure the community is well engaged and consulted on completing the form."

The Census has been conducted in Australia for more than a century , but this will be the third time Norfolk Island has ever participated in the survey. It also marks a decade since the Australian government passed reforms that led to the island being included in the Census.

In 1914, Norfolk became an Australian territory, but the "precise constitutional arrangement was not clear at the time", according to an online statement by legal advisory firm Norfolk Advisory.

Around 65 years later, the Australian parliament allowed Norfolk Islanders to form a limited self-government. Following governance reforms passed in 2015 and implemented in 2016, the Australian government assumed responsibility for the island's governance.

In 2023, Norfolk Island regained some involvement in its affairs through the establishment of a new advisory body, the Norfolk Island Governance Committee. The island is now considered an external territory of Australia.

title.en: 'We had no intention': Israeli ambassador defends rare move on Labor platform
title.zh: “我们无意为之”：以色列大使为在工党平台上的罕见举动辩护

summary.en: Following criticism, Israel's ambassador to Australia defended their engagement with the Labor platform, stating their intention was solely to present facts to decision-makers.
summary.zh: 在受到批评后，以色列驻澳大利亚大使为其与工党平台接触的举动进行了辩护，称其目的只是向决策者提供事实。

body.en:
Israel's ambassador to Australia has defended his embassy's unusual public intervention ahead of Labor's national conference last month, rejecting suggestions it sought to influence the party's platform and insisting it was merely providing information to decision-makers.

In a rare step, the Israeli embassy issued a lengthy statement ahead of the conference in Adelaide, taking issue with Labor's proposed position on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

The embassy argued Labor's draft national platform placed responsibility for the conflict on Israel while overlooking the role of Hamas and Palestinian leadership.

It sparked criticism from pro-Palestinian advocates that Israel was inappropriately interfering in Australian politics.

Speaking to SBS Hebrew on Thursday, Israeli ambassador Hillel Newman said "we had no intention and no actual intervention".

"All we did was we put forth facts for the decision-makers to have before them in making educated decisions," he said.

"We are just a resource of some kind in giving the information. We did not intervene in the convention itself. We do not intervene in the process. We just brought information to the knowledge of the decision-makers.

"The Palestinian envoys here also had some things to say about the ALP platform and convention, and no-one said it's foreign intervention," he said.

At the time, the Australia Palestine Advocacy Network (APAN), an advocacy group, condemned what it called an "extraordinary intervention" by the Israeli embassy and described it as "an unacceptable attempt by a foreign government to influence Australia’s domestic political processes".

"If the Israeli regime believes Labor's platform is too critical while Gaza is being destroyed, perhaps it should reflect on its own conduct rather than attempting to pressure an Australian political party," APAN president Nasser Mashni said.

Mashni said the draft platform fell "far short of taking appropriate action to recognise the Palestinian genocide".

Israel has been accused of genocide by a United Nations inquiry, an allegation it denies. Its prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is the subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, which Israel rejects.

The Labor platform is debated at its national conference to determine the party's positions on a broad range of issues. Its 2026 draft reflected shifts and an expanded position on Israel and Palestine since its last iteration in 2023.

The government decided to recognise Palestinian statehood in September last year.

reflection.en: In public discourse, the call to speak truth is vital, yet what constitutes 'facts' and how they are received can be complex.
